FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
CONTACT: Hilary Black, 604-783-4137
April 11, 2001
VANCOUVER –

While the Minister of Health Alan Rock and his assistant, David Herferd, consulted with representatives of the West Coast Compassion Clubs yesterday, Richmond Police raided the farm of the BC Compassion Club Society's (BCCCS) contracted not-for-profit cannabis supplier. Health Canada not only learned from the Clubs' collective experiences, but also witnessed the archaic and repressive conditions under which the clubs are supplying cannabis to those in medical need.

The Minister requested a meeting with Hilary Black of the BCCCS and Philip Lucas of the Vancouver Island Compassion Society in order to gather information from the most experienced medical marijuana distributors and producers. The Minister was specifically interested in information on the production of medical cannabis. Ironically, as that valuable information was being shared, Black received a phone call informing her that one of the BCCCS's contracted production sites was being raided by the police.

Police confiscated 1000 plants that would have supplied the club's 1400 members with low cost, high quality medicinal cannabis. The Compassion Club was helping with production costs, in exchange for access to the medical grade cannabis that Dr. Paul Hornby, an accomplished herbal medicine researcher, was producing for research purposes. Two volunteer gardeners were arrested along with Hornby, who has a license from Health Canada to possess and produce cannabis. The address on the license was that of his lab, but the greenhouse was located on his research farm. Dr. Hornby had received legal advice that the license would apply to the farm because his company owned both properties.

" They held my five year old-son and sixty-five year old mother-in-law at gun point, " said an emotional and distraught Hornby. Hilary Black of the BCCCS explained, " The true harm of cannabis stems from its illegal status. That little boy is in shock today. Why? Because the whole family is being persecuted for Paul's belief in herbal medicines. " The three were charged with possession and production and released last night.

The BCCCS has been leading the way for the last four years in providing marijuana to Canadians in medical need. The BCCCS welcomed the opportunity to assist the Minister and also to give him preliminary feedback on the proposed guidelines that were released on Saturday. Hilary Black, spokesperson for the BCCCS, asserted their position on the proposed guidelines. Black stated " We cannot support the creation of a costly and
unnecessary bureaucracy to authorize access to an herb that is far less toxic than most over the counter medications. "

The BCCCS will be identifying other major concerns in their recommendations later this month, and will be participating in the creation of distribution guidelines in August. In the meantime the BCCCS will continue to dance between advising Health Canada and dealing with police persecution.
